The target video uses live-action cinematic conference imagery with restrained camera movement, clean stage lighting, and stable spatial continuity. Every visual event is concrete and directly observable.
[Shot 1] A tight centered 50mm shot in <Subject 1> holds on the main LED screen with a static camera. The screen becomes pure black. Three broad solid white horizontal rectangles appear one after another across the upper-middle area, evenly spaced and identical in style. One thin solid white rectangular bar appears beneath them. The finished screen composition contains only these four simple geometric light shapes against the black background. The shapes stay flat, uniform, and motionless through the end of the shot.
[Shot 2] At 00:05.000, the shot cuts to a centered medium 35mm view in <Subject 1>. The stage-wing side door is built directly into the wing at the immediate edge of the performance stage, with a very short threshold connecting the doorway to the stage floor. The door opens inward slowly to about seventy degrees. Through the open doorway, the visible area consists of the empty threshold, the adjacent wing wall, and the immediate stage floor, and this empty architectural view remains unchanged for the rest of the shot. A single focused spotlight at the stage edge switches on and gradually brightens across the empty side-stage floor. The camera pushes forward with small amplitude at slow speed while preserving the direct physical connection between doorway and stage edge. If the main LED screen remains visible in the background, it keeps the same black field with the same four simple geometric light shapes established in [Shot 1].
